summary: Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) was a philosopher who studied at Collegium Fridericianum and the University of Königsberg (1740–1746). He held the chair of logic and metaphysics at Königsberg from 1770 and taught Johann Gottfried von Herder.
Imran Philip works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Kaustubh Mani Sengupta and held a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Imre Bangha is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University. He held positions at Visva-Bharati, Oxford and Wolfson College (around 2003), and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Imre Galambos works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Eötvös Loránd, Nankai, and UC Berkeley, he held posts at UC Santa Barbara, the British Library, Cambridge, Zhejiang University, and Hamburg.

Imre Hamar is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki. He was a visiting professor at Otani University (~1997–1998) and became professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006.

In-gun Kang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Kang studied at the Jesuit School of Theology, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under multiple teachers, and Heythrop College under Michael Barnes (attested 2012).

Ines Konczak is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She served as a postdoctoral research fellow at the Berlin State Museums and as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012.
Ingmar Heise works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies at Leiden University by 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch is an Indologist, Buddhologist, and linguist who earned his PhD at Freie Universität Berlin in 2000. He taught Andrea Schlosser and Kathrin Holz and held a professorship at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018).
Inyoung Chung is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) was a religious studies and history scholar. Educated at Bucharest, Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, Paris-Sorbonne, and under Mircea Eliade, he held posts at the University of Groningen and the University of Chicago Divinity School.
Iona Macgregor is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).
Ippei Okamoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Toyo University (attested 2014) and Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala (1884–1956) was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian specialist. He served as Professor of Iranian Studies at Deccan College (~1939–1942) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (~1953–1956), teaching Sukumar Sen and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.

Irawati Karve (1905–1970) was an Indologist and historian. After studying at Fergusson College and the University of Mumbai under G. S. Ghurye, she held posts at Deccan College (~1939–1970) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1951–1952).

Irfan Habib is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (~1947–1953), and New College, Oxford (~1954–1958), and has worked as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1953.

Irving Babbitt (1865–1933) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Educated at Williams College, Harvard, and the University of Paris, he taught at Williams College (~1893–1894) and Harvard University (~1894–1933), where his students included Wu Mi and Yongtong Tang.

Isaac Schapera (1905–2003) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the London School of Economics, later holding posts at Cape Town, Chicago, Toronto, and LSE (~1950–1969).

Isaak Jakob Schmidt (1779–1847) was a scholar of Tibetology, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies who received a doctorate from Rostock (1823). He held positions with the Russian Bible Society and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy is a Tibetologist who studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, EPHE, Harvard, and Tibet University, working under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She has taught anthropology at Laval University (~2004, 2007).
